chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Saʿīd, who said:

I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), and I said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you. In all matters they sought to extinguish your light and to demean you, until they lodged you in this most repulsive inn, the inn of the vagabonds.”

So he said: “Here, O Ibn Saʿīd.” Then he gestured with his hand and said: “Look.” So I looked, and there I was amidst elegant gardens and radiant gardens, in which were excellent fragrant ones, and youths as though they were hidden pearls, and birds, and gazelles, and rivers gushing forth. Then my sight was bewildered and my eye grew weary.
So he said: “Wherever we may be, this is made ready for us; we are not in the inn of the vagabonds.”

key_terms.إِطْفَاءَ نُورِكَ: attempting to extinguish the Imam’s light, meaning to suppress his divine guidance and manifest rank
key_terms.اللُّؤْلُؤُ الْمَكْنُونُ: hidden pearls, describing the purity and beauty of the youths seen in the vision
key_terms.الْخَانَ الْأَشْنَعَ: the most repulsive inn, indicating an outwardly degrading place of lodging
key_terms.بِرَوْضَاتٍ آنِقَاتٍ: amidst elegant gardens, referring to a beautiful unseen garden-like realm
key_terms.خَانَ الصَّعَالِيكِ: the inn of vagabonds or destitute people, used here to describe social humiliation
key_terms.عَتِيدٌ: prepared and made ready, indicating what has been readied for the Imam (عليه السلام)

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the unseen dignity and divine station of Imam Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) despite worldly humiliation?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how Imam Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), despite being placed in a degrading lodging by his enemies, disclosed to Ṣāliḥ ibn Saʿīd a hidden realm of splendid gardens and blessings prepared for him. It highlights the exalted rank of the Imam (عليه السلام) and shows that outward humiliation does not diminish the divine honor and unseen station granted to the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام).

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salih Bin Saeed who said,

‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, so I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! In every affair they are intending to extinguish your<sup>asws</sup> Light and be deficient with you<sup>asws</sup>, to the extent that they have lodged you<sup>asws</sup> in this repulsive inn, and inn for the tramps!’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Over here, you (look), O Ibn Saeed!. Then he<sup>asws</sup> gestured by his<sup>asws</sup> hand and said: ‘Look!’ So I looked, and there I was in delightful gardens, captivating gardens, wherein were Bounties, female and male servants, as if they were hidden pearls, and birds, and deers, and rivers gushing forth. So my sight was bewildered and my eyes were dulled.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Wherever we<sup>asws</sup> may be, so this is prepared for us<sup>asws</sup>. We<sup>asws</sup> aren’t in the inn of the tramps’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Khayrana Ali-Asbati who has said the following.
“Once I went to al-Madina to see abu al-Hassan (a.s.).

He asked me, “What is the news from Ali-Wathiq (Abbassid ruler)?” I said, may Allah take my soul in service for your cause, I left him in good health and I am of all people the latest who met him. I met him just ten days ago.” The narrator has said that the Imam (a.s.) then said, “People of al-Madina say that he has died.” When he said, “people say’ I understood that it is he himself. He then said, “What has Ja‘far (Mutawakkil Abbassid) done?” I said, “I left him in the worst condition of all people. He was in prison.” The narrator has said that he then said, “He has become the ruler. What has ibn Ali-Zayyat (the vizir of Wathiq) has done?” I said, may Allah take my soul in service for your cause, people are with him and whatever he says it goes.” The narrator has said that he then said, “His progress has proved to become a misfortune for him.” The narrator has said that he then paused for a while and said to me, “The measures of Allah, the Most High and His decrees must go on. O Khayaran, al-Wathiq has died and Ali-Mutawakkil , Ja‘far has replaced him and ibn al-Zayyat is killed.” I then asked, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, when this has happened?” He said, “After six days from the time you left.”
